title: Derived sections through finite pushforward for module sheaves
statement:
Let $\Lambda$ be a commutative ring, $p:Z\to Y$ a finite morphism of schemes [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism], and $M$ a bounded-below complex of sheaves of $\Lambda$-modules on the small etale site of $Z$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-site, def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Direct image $p_*$ on these module sheaves is exact and sends injective objects to injective objects. There is a canonical natural isomorphism $\lambda_{p,M}:R\Gamma(Y,p_*M)\xrightarrow{\sim}R\Gamma(Z,M)$ [def-kun-rgamma-unbounded]. Its normalization is: for a bounded-below injective resolution $M\to L$, $p_*L$ is a bounded-below injective resolution of $p_*M$, and $\lambda_{p,M}$ is induced by $\Gamma(Y,p_*L)=\Gamma(Z,L)$.

For an arbitrary scheme morphism $h:Y'\to Y$, form $Z'=Y'\times_Y Z$ with projections $g:Z'\to Z$ and $p':Z'\to Y'$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. Let $\beta_M:h^{-1}p_*M\to p'_*g^{-1}M$ be the adjoint of the counit map $(p')^{-1}h^{-1}p_*M=g^{-1}p^{-1}p_*M\to g^{-1}M$; inverse image and these adjunctions are the exact module functors of [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact]. The square with horizontal arrows $\lambda_{p,M}$ and $\lambda_{p',g^{-1}M}$ and vertical arrows
$$R\Gamma(Y,p_*M)\xrightarrow{\mathrm{res}_h}R\Gamma(Y',h^{-1}p_*M)\xrightarrow{R\Gamma(\beta_M)}R\Gamma(Y',p'_*g^{-1}M),\qquad R\Gamma(Z,M)\xrightarrow{\mathrm{res}_g}R\Gamma(Z',g^{-1}M)$$
commutes in $D(\operatorname{Mod}\Lambda)$. Here restriction is the map induced by the inverse-image/direct-image unit. Only the displayed canonical mate is used; no base-change isomorphism is a hypothesis of this compatibility assertion.

proof.text: A bounded-below termwise-injective complex is K-injective. Direct image preserves its lower bound, quasi-isomorphisms and injective terms, so its sections unit is invertible as well. Expand the defining right-derived composition comparison and its unit factorization; transport from the homotopy quotient to complexes to obtain finite Leray normalization. Naturality and cancellation of Q(i) and its inverse prove the normalization for every resolution appearing in the unchanged statement. Use the existing exposed comp_fac and comp_unit_app helpers of Sheaf.Paper.DerivedLerayComp.

proof.text: The ordinary direct-image composition and terminal-section comparisons associate: after evaluating on the terminal object both maps are equal by terminality. Apply rightDerived_ext with the iterated composite right-derived unit. The derived unit factorization equations reduce both resulting maps to the localized ordinary equality. Conjugacy of composition identifies this canonical derived comparison with rightDerivedLowerStarComp. Combining its unit-conjugation equation with naturality of Leray proves composition of the unit-Leray restriction transformations. Import the already proved comp_fac and comp_unit_app from Sheaf.Paper.DerivedLerayComp, and its derived_comp_eq generalized in place to any Grothendieck abelian coefficient category. Only the remaining module-coefficient composition and restriction arguments need private helpers here; the AddCommGrp theorem in the imported module retains its original signature.

proof.text: Compare the finite exact derived adjunction with the exact-left/right-derived adjunction transported along the exact direct-image comparison. Localization extensionality and the two unit-factorization equations identify their units, hence the adjunctions. Its triangle identity identifies restriction along a finite map followed by sections of its counit with the published finite Leray comparison.

proof.text: The derived square is the descent of the two inverse-image composition isomorphisms, so composition of restriction gives its restriction-square equation. In the desired mate square substitute the counit formula for finite Leray on the base-changed map. Naturality carries the mate through restriction; mateEquiv_counit replaces its transpose by the square comparison followed by pullback of the original counit. The restriction-square equation, naturality, and the original counit description of finite Leray give exactly the stated equality. Finite base change supplies finiteness of the new vertical map; no invertibility of the mate is assumed or proved.
